name: Miro Assist
description: Miro Assist was the former name of Miro's in-product generative AI feature, now presented as Miro AI for creating, summarizing, clustering, translating, refining, and organizing content on Miro boards.
agentUseSummary: Miro Assist cannot be connected or installed as a separate Relay provider. Use the canonical Miro provider only for its currently supported bounded board and item REST actions; those scopes do not authorize the current Miro AI feature. Relay must not automate Miro's signed-in AI interface or treat the separately documented Miro MCP Server as an Assist credential until product, security, privacy, policy, and runtime owners approve a canonical Miro expansion.

blocked.label: Create a separate Miro Assist connection
blocked.description: Miro Assist is a historical feature name inside Miro, not a distinct provider account, app authority, token lifecycle, or resource system.

blocked.label: Run Miro Assist or Miro AI actions
blocked.description: Generating, editing, summarizing, clustering, translating, analyzing, or synthesizing board content through Miro AI is not authorized by Relay's existing boards:read and boards:write REST connection.

blocked.label: Automate the signed-in Miro AI interface
blocked.description: Browser automation, session cookies, passwords, verification codes, private endpoints, undocumented requests, and scraping of Miro's in-product AI experience are blocked.

blocked.label: Mount Miro MCP as Miro Assist
blocked.description: Miro's official MCP Server is a separate OAuth 2.1 AI-client gateway with curated tools, team binding, plan limits, and admin controls; Relay must evaluate it as an expansion of canonical Miro rather than silently substituting it for this historical feature name.

blocked.label: Administer Miro AI
blocked.description: Changing AI capabilities, model selection, moderation, data-use settings, team eligibility, plan, add-ons, credits, billing, or enterprise controls is outside this provider boundary.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No Miro Assist action is enabled because the historical name identifies an in-product Miro AI feature and no approved Relay external contract currently exposes it.

runtimeSupport.description: No Miro Assist or Miro AI tools are mounted. OpenClaw may use only the canonical Miro provider's currently approved bounded REST tools.
No Miro Assist or Miro AI tools are mounted. Hermes may use only the canonical Miro provider's currently approved bounded REST tools.

providerSetup.blocker: Miro Assist was an in-product AI feature and is now Miro AI. Miro documents it for members in browser, desktop, and mobile clients with plan eligibility, shared AI credits, admin capability controls, model processing, moderation, and data-use rules. Relay's canonical Miro OAuth app exposes bounded REST board and item operations under boards:read and boards:write; those scopes and endpoints do not publish a Miro AI generation or analysis contract. Miro now separately publishes an MCP Server for external AI clients at mcp.miro.com using OAuth 2.1, dynamic client registration, one-team authorization, curated board tools, plan limits, and enterprise enablement. That gateway is a possible canonical Miro expansion, not a distinct Miro Assist provider, and has not been approved or implemented in Relay.
providerSetup.nextAction: Keep this historical feature slug non-installable. Product, security, privacy, legal, AI governance, runtime, and customer owners must decide whether canonical Miro should add its official MCP Server. If approved, freeze dynamic registration and OAuth lifecycle, team and board binding, exact tool schemas, read and mutation limits, approval profiles, AI-credit consumption, model and data-processing disclosures, enterprise enablement, audit, redaction, revocation, rate limits, retention, and failure behavior. Implement and validate that work under canonical Miro rather than creating Miro Assist credentials or automating the signed-in feature.

evidence.supports: Miro's launch announcement describes Miro Assist as its beta AI partner embedded in Miro for generating ideas, extracting board insights, and transforming content into presentations and mind maps.

Miro's current help center presents Miro AI as a suite of in-product features for team members on browser, desktop, and mobile, including creation, summarization, diagrams, translation, clustering, and canvas analysis.
Miro documents shared plan-based AI credits, monthly limits, add-ons, and per-action consumption for current Miro AI features.
Miro documents company-admin controls for feature availability, team eligibility, model-backed capabilities, and moderation inside Miro AI.
Miro's public REST platform uses app OAuth and explicit scopes to access board data and does not publish Miro Assist or Miro AI generation and analysis endpoints in its resource API contract.

Miro separately documents an official MCP Server for external AI clients with OAuth 2.1, dynamic client registration, board-permission enforcement, curated tools, team authorization, plan limits, and enterprise admin enablement.

Miro's developer policy requires consent, least-privilege scopes, current data access, secure handling, accurate branding, and prohibits using APIs or SDKs to circumvent limitations or replicate core Miro services.
